# The calendar's header names the period it shows

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context

Clio's look read of PR #21913, the Calendar year example of #21889 ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21913#issuecomment-7079503389)): a click on a day in the year view opens the day view, and the day view says only "Wed 22". Nothing on screen says it is 22 July 2026. It became its own leaf because the cause sits in the calendar's header, not in the example.

## The Problem

On `dev` `50fcfc526c`:

- **The header has no period.** `Neo.calendar.view.MainContainer#createHeaderItems()` builds two toolbars: the side-panel toggle with ‹ Today ›, and the view buttons. No item shows the date or range on screen.
- **The week and day views name weekdays only.** Their column headers come from `intlFormat_day = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {weekday})` plus the day of the month (`src/calendar/view/week/Component.mjs`, `afterSetDayNameFormat` and the header build). A week that spans two months does not say so, and a single day has no month or year.

So a visitor who navigates with ‹ › or arrives from the year view has to count to know where they are.

## The Architectural Reality

- `currentDate` lives in the calendar's state provider. The year view, the date selector and the interval buttons all read and write it there. `activeView` is a reactive config of `MainContainer`.
- A component in the header can bind `currentDate` the way the date selector does (`bind: {value: data => …data.currentDate}`), and follow `activeView` from `afterSetActiveView`.
- `locale` is in the provider too, and the views format with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

## The Fix

A period label in the calendar's header, between the interval navigation and the view buttons, formatted per view in the calendar's `locale`:

| View | Example (`en-US`) |
|---|---|
| Day | Wednesday, July 22, 2026 |
| Week | Jul 19 – 25, 2026 (across months: Jun 28 – Jul 4, 2026) |
| Month | July 2026 |
| Year | none: the year view names its year |

At phone width it takes a short form (for example "Jul 22, 2026"), and the view buttons keep their row.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In Day, Week and Month views the header names the period on screen, and it follows ‹, Today, › and a day click in the year view.
- [ ] The label follows the calendar's `locale`.
- [ ] At 390 × 844 the header still fits without wrapping the view buttons.
- [ ] A spec covers the label for each view.
- [ ] The look: Day, Week and Month at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844 in Neo Dark, on the pull request.

## Out of Scope

The year view's own header. The week and day column headers. The date selector in the side panel.

  2. Will render both full and compact (`short` month, no weekday) period spans / responsive header rules so `390 × 844` keeps the view buttons on one unclipped row without horizontal overflow, verified in Playwright at `1440 × 900` and `390 × 844`.
